head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e
notes: Premise ok: HEAD pinned at 1f725ce, base b4981b8 is an ancestor, overlay applied (apply -R --check exit 0). All 48 chunk files read in full; no partners. Go guide context/rules/go.md read. Known ledger consulted: the many open code-style rows for this chunk (NIT-2..43-r1, NIT-18..26-r2, NIT-166..174-r1) were not re-reported. Legacy patterns left out per the go.md ENFORCEMENT clause: literal 200 status codes in config_sync_test.go (file-wide pre-existing), '64 KiB' literal in the style-size error (mirrors routines.go:442), routineModelDefault const placed among type blocks in routines.go (file already mixes consts after types). Cross-chunk / other-direction suspicions for the station: (1) handleSessionsArchiveTab sets Title "Sessions — archive" untranslated while handleSessionsScope translates "Sessions" — the casual German <title> stays English (i18n correctness, not style); (2) layout.html now shows the Welcome nav entry to casual audiences (dropped isDeveloperAudience gate) while welcome.html's bootstrap section text is English-only and untranslated — check against the casual/i18n spec.

findings.fix: Drop the in-body comment at bootstrap.go:78-79 (bootstrapDeadline already names the bound), or at least remove the hard-coded '6h' so it cannot drift from the constant.
findings.claim: The in-body comment above the exec.CommandContext call restates the bootstrapDeadline constant and hard-codes its value ('bounded at 6h'), so it adds no intent the name lacks and goes stale the moment bootstrapDeadline (line 19) changes.
findings.evidence: Re-read bootstrap.go at 1f725ce: line 19 declares const bootstrapDeadline = 6 * time.Hour; lines 78-79 read '// Multi-hour child under its own backstop deadline (the routinewrap pattern): // bounded at 6h, far above any real bootstrap run.' directly above context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), bootstrapDeadline) on line 81. Concrete sequence: change bootstrapDeadline to 12*time.Hour and the comment still says 6h. Not a known-ledger entry (NIT-29-r1 covers the bootstrapEnv grouping comments, NIT-14-r1 the call layout).

findings.fix: In revert-expands-install-markers build the server with newSectionServer(t, live, fragment) and read server.settingsPath instead of re-inlining its body, and extract the duplicated install.env + t.Chdir setup (lines 121-123 and 142-144) into one t.Helper (e.g. chdirInstallEnv(t, "PEEK_CONTROL_PORT=42542\n")).
findings.claim: The two new subtests duplicate setup code: revert-expands-install-markers (lines 125-130) re-inlines newSectionServer's body (TempDir, settings.json/fragment.json paths, two WriteFiles, newTestServer) only to keep livePath, which the server already exposes as settingsPath, and the install.env + t.Chdir block is copied verbatim in both subtests.
findings.evidence: Re-read config_sync_test.go at 1f725ce: newSectionServer (lines 28-36) does exactly dir := t.TempDir(); livePath/fragmentPath joins; two os.WriteFile; newTestServer(&Options{ClaudeFragmentPath, SettingsPath}); lines 125-130 repeat those six statements byte-for-byte modulo the JSON literals; lines 121-123 and 142-144 are identical (TempDir, WriteFile install.env with PEEK_CONTROL_PORT=42542, t.Chdir). A change to the marker fixture (e.g. a second install.env key) must be edited in two places. Not in the known ledger (tests-NIT-7-r2 is about missing marker coverage in config.go, not this duplication).

findings.fix: Declare saveProfileSelection(audience string, devMode bool, language string) and writeFileAtomic(content, path string), updating the callers in profilesettings.go:89, presentation.go:106/115 and presentation_test.go:355.
findings.claim: Two new functions in presentation.go declare their parameters out of alphabetical order: saveProfileSelection(audience, language string, devMode bool) (line 88) and writeFileAtomic(path, content string) (line 200).
findings.evidence: Re-read presentation.go at 1f725ce: line 88 'func (st *presentationStore) saveProfileSelection(audience, language string, devMode bool) error' (alphabetical: audience, devMode, language); line 200 'func writeFileAtomic(path, content string) error' (alphabetical: content, path). Both functions are new in this diff. The same diff applies RULE-GOLANG-CALL-003 elsewhere (proposalViews/groupViews reordered to active, file(s), language, refs, tab, votes; sentimentTrend(language, points); signalDetail(date, language); batchBands(batches, language)), so this is a regression, not legacy. Known code-style-NIT-13-r1 flags only bootstrapEnv in bootstrap.go; NIT-11-r1 on writeFileAtomic is about duplication, not parameter order.

findings.fix: Extract a (s *Server) nightlyRoutine() (*routines.Routine, error) helper doing routines.Scan + slices.IndexFunc on nightlyRoutineName, and call it from both styleTestTarget and checkNightlyRoutine (welcome.go:116-128).
findings.claim: styleTestTarget re-implements checkNightlyRoutine's lookup of the nightly routine — routines.Scan(s.routinesDir), slices.IndexFunc matching routine.Name == nightlyRoutineName, index < 0 bail-out — instead of sharing it.
findings.evidence: Re-read profilesettings.go at 1f725ce lines 189-198: 'list, err := routines.Scan(s.routinesDir)' / 'index := slices.IndexFunc(list, func(routine routines.Routine) bool { return routine.Name == nightlyRoutineName })' / 'if index < 0 { return target }'; welcome.go lines 116-128 carry the identical Scan + IndexFunc closure + index < 0 sequence. Both run on the same server state; a change to how the nightly routine is located (e.g. honoring a renamed or duplicated routine) must be made twice. Not in the known ledger (code-style-NIT-28-r1 covers the claude-envelope parse duplication in profileTestAnswer, a different block).

findings.fix: Bind the slice first — statuses := []repos.WorktreeStatus{{Branch: "claude/feature"}, {Branch: "claude/keep"}} — and call server.statusCache.Store("demo", "", statuses), as the sibling skip-output-leaves-cache-untouched subtest already does.
findings.claim: The new clean-removal-drops-cached-rows subtest passes a multi-line []repos.WorktreeStatus composite literal inline as the third argument of server.statusCache.Store.
findings.evidence: Re-read repos_test.go at 1f725ce lines 523-526: 'server.statusCache.Store("demo", "", []repos.WorktreeStatus{' / '{Branch: "claude/feature"},' / '{Branch: "claude/keep"},' / '})'. The very next new subtest (lines 540-541) binds 'statuses := []repos.WorktreeStatus{{Branch: "claude/feature"}}' before calling Store, so the two new subtests disagree on the rule. Not in the known ledger (code-style-NIT-41-r1 is the statuses declaration inside a t.Run body at line 287).

findings.fix: Declare Store(fingerprint, repoName string, statuses []repos.WorktreeStatus) and DropBranches(branches []string, repoName string), updating the callers in repos.go:363/513 and the cache tests.
findings.claim: The new statusCache methods declare parameters out of alphabetical order: Store(repoName, fingerprint string, statuses ...) at line 68 and DropBranches(repoName string, branches []string) at line 44.
findings.evidence: Re-read statuscache.go at 1f725ce: line 44 'func (c *statusCache) DropBranches(repoName string, branches []string)' (alphabetical: branches, repoName); line 68 'func (c *statusCache) Store(repoName, fingerprint string, statuses []repos.WorktreeStatus) statusEntry' (alphabetical: fingerprint, repoName, statuses). statuscache.go is a new file in this diff, and the same diff reorders proposalViews/groupViews/sentimentTrend parameters alphabetically, so the rule is live here. Not in the known ledger (NIT-6-r1/NIT-7-r1 on this file cover type order and the mu comment).

findings.fix: Bind statuses := []repos.WorktreeStatus{{Branch: "claude/alpha"}} and pass statuses to cache.Store, matching lines 17-18 and 36-41 of the same file.
findings.claim: TestStatusCacheDelete passes a []repos.WorktreeStatus composite literal inline as a call argument to cache.Store.
findings.evidence: Re-read statuscache_test.go at 1f725ce line 61: 'cache.Store("demo", "fp-1", []repos.WorktreeStatus{{Branch: "claude/alpha"}})'. The other two tests in this new file bind the literal first (line 17 'first := ...', line 27 'second := ...', line 36 'statuses := ...') and pass the variable, so the file is internally inconsistent on RULE-GOLANG-CALL-005. Not in the known ledger.

findings.fix: Rename the spacing class to what it is (e.g. .op-form-row in style.css:354, applied in sessions_index.html:20 and _worktree_status.html:27), or give the archive form its own class instead of class="reload-form".
findings.claim: The 'Reload from disk' form was replaced by the 'Archive folder' form, but the new form keeps class="reload-form", so the archive control is styled under a class named for the removed reload feature.
findings.evidence: Re-read sessions_index.html at 1f725ce line 20: '<form class="reload-form" hx-post="/sessions/{{pathEscape .Scope.Name}}/archive" ... hx-confirm="{{t \"Archive this folder? ...\"}}">' wrapping '{{t "Archive folder"}}'; the diff removed '<form hx-post="/sessions/reload" ... class="reload-form">' with its Reload-from-disk button and the POST /sessions/reload route. style.css:354 defines '.reload-form { margin-bottom: 16px; }', also used by the worktree Reload button wrapper (_worktree_status.html:27), so on this page the name now describes a feature that no longer exists. Not in the known ledger.
